name: Button
summary: Use a button to let a user perform a clear action, such as saving information or continuing to the next step.
whenToUse: Use the default button for the primary action on a page or form.
Use a start button for the entry point to a transactional service.
Use secondary or warning variants only when the action hierarchy or destructive consequence requires them.
whenNotToUse: Do not use a button for ordinary navigation; use a link unless the link is the explicit start of a service.
Do not place several visually primary buttons together when one action is the clear next step.
Do not use the warning variant for a reversible or low-risk action.

anatomy.name: Native action element
anatomy.description: Use a button element for actions and form submission. A start-page link may use button styling with link semantics made explicit.

anatomy.name: Action label
anatomy.description: Short sentence-case text describes the action and its effect.

anatomy.name: GOV.UK module hook
anatomy.description: The data-module attribute allows GOV.UK Frontend to attach its supported behaviour.

variants.name: Default
variants.use: The page's main action, for example “Save and continue”.

variants.name: Secondary
variants.use: A less prominent action, for example “Find address” or “Save as draft”.

variants.name: Warning
variants.use: A destructive action with serious consequences, for example “Delete account”.

variants.name: Start
variants.use: The single entry point to a service, labelled “Start now”.

behaviour: Initialise GOV.UK Frontend JavaScript when using data-module="govuk-button".
Form buttons should declare an appropriate type; use type="submit" for submission and type="button" for client-side actions.
The interface must remain understandable if JavaScript does not run.
accessibility: Prefer the native button element for actions so keyboard and assistive-technology behaviour is supplied by the browser.
If a service-start link is styled as a button, retain an href and use the official start-button markup.
Do not encode action meaning through colour alone; the label must describe the consequence.
Preserve the official focus treatment and do not remove the visible focus indicator.
content: Start with a verb and describe the action, such as “Continue”, “Save and continue”, or “Delete account”.
Avoid vague labels such as “Submit” when a more specific action can be named.

htmlExamples.name: Default submit button
htmlExamples.html:
<button type="submit" class="govuk-button" data-module="govuk-button">
  Save and continue
</button>

htmlExamples.name: Secondary button
htmlExamples.html:
<button type="submit" class="govuk-button govuk-button--secondary" data-module="govuk-button">
  Find address
</button>

htmlExamples.name: Warning button
htmlExamples.html:
<button type="submit" class="govuk-button govuk-button--warning" data-module="govuk-button">
  Delete account
</button>
